clue.text: Exuberant actors recoiled in false show of emotion

indicators.note: exuberant suggests unrestrained, lively behaviour, so the two fodder words are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Over-the-top performers flinched in a fake display of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to insincere weeping, after the old belief that the reptile wept while eating its prey.

clue.text: Sticky stuff keeps son in check

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to check or restrain is to rein in
S is the standard genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Some gummy substance helps a parent keep their boy under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree sap that hardens is the classic gummy, adhesive material.

clue.text: Picasso, for instance, succeeded in old measure

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for succeeded within the old length unit

parts.note: a cubit is an ancient unit of length, roughly forearm length
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: The great Spanish painter did well using an antique unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded the Cubism movement, so he is an example of a painter of that school.

clue.text: Bowler's tally in local contest

parts.note: a bowler hat is called a derby, chiefly in America
to tally is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's score in a neighbourhood fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket but is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between two nearby rival teams, such as two clubs from the same city, is called this.

clue.text: Sets down poems

definitions.meaning: short narrative songs or ballads, as in medieval verse

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb meaning places and a plural noun for ballads or songs.

clue.text: Troon WI misused golf club

indicators.note: misused signals the letters are put to the wrong use, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Women's Institute members at the Troon course misuse one of their clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish golf course; the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: This long iron is one of the set of sticks a golfer carries, now rarely used.

clue.text: Australian landmark broadcasts on radio with popular music

indicators.note: on radio signals that the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it
rock is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: An Aussie landmark gets transmitted on the wireless with chart songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant red sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory, now Uluru, is the country's best-known natural sight.

clue.text: Reporter at Olympics, perhaps, could make last sprint go with it

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be formed into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A journalist at the Games might turn the final dash into a race start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' suggests a journalist but means something that makes a loud report, a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun fired to begin a race makes a report, so at an athletics meet it is a reporter in that sense.

clue.text: Mini riot breaking out with bishop banning alcohol

indicators.note: breaking out suggests things bursting apart and scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small disturbance erupts alongside a cleric in a dry campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy or advocacy of outlawing the sale of drink, as in 1920s America.

clue.text: Criticise Mary who cooks on TV, receiving small sound of disapproval

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the small letter goes inside

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise sharply
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
Mary Berry is a well-known British television cook and baking judge

explanation.surface: Knocking a TV cook while she gets a little tut of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing this rude noise with the tongue and lips expresses contempt; it is also called a Bronx cheer.

clue.text: Policeman getting tip off on Her Majesty — a work for the Met?

indicators.note: tip off says the first letter, the tip, is removed

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An officer gets a hint about the Queen, a job for London's police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Met' looks like London's Metropolitan Police; here it is New York's Metropolitan Opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged musical drama is the kind of piece performed at New York's famous Metropolitan house.

clue.text: Get keen on messy place coming clean

parts.note: to hone a blade is to make it keen, sharp
a sty, a pigsty, is a byword for a filthy place

explanation.surface: Being eager to tidy up a dirty spot by cleaning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like eager but is sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up and telling the truth is the virtue of truthfulness.

clue.text: Advertising European TV with channel already selected?

parts.note: PR, public relations, covers publicity and promotion
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A television ad from Europe comes with its station already tuned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stored station on a radio or TV, fixed in advance so one button recalls it.

clue.text: Soldiers taking German gentleman in old military vehicles

indicators.note: in places the German title within the vehicles

parts.note: tanks are armoured military vehicles
Herr is the German for Mr, a gentleman

explanation.surface: Troops take a German man in their old armoured vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A British army term for all soldiers who are not commissioned officers.

clue.text: Polish expert

definitions.meaning: to polish or shine something by rubbing
an enthusiast who knows a lot, as in a film fan

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rubbing to a shine and a noun for a keen, knowledgeable enthusiast.

clue.text: Member of society that's dispensed with forenames

indicators.note: dispensed means distributed or given out, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a secretive club who has done away with first names.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the fraternal order of the Craft, a famously secretive society.

clue.text: Toast in base tent, foolishly — take precautions!

indicators.note: in puts the drinking toast inside the rearranged letters
foolishly suggests something done wrongly or in a muddle, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a drinking toast said before downing a glass

explanation.surface: Raising a glass at camp, recklessly, then being told to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like bread or a verb, but it is the drinker's cry before emptying a glass, which the shuffled camp letters wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical idiom means prepare for a storm or trouble, originally by securing a ship's openings.

clue.text: See 17
Want expert to limit cattle disease heading north

indicators.note: to limit means to bound or enclose, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: heading means going in front of, so the disease letters come before the compass point

parts.note: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A skilled person is needed to contain mad cow disease spreading northward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of something, as in for want of a nail, is a non-presence.

clue.text: Leave out captain?

definitions.meaning: a skipper, a team or ship's captain, is often shortened to this

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to omit and is also a short informal name for the leader of a team or boat.

clue.text: Scarf on top of neck is hot

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn round the shoulders

indicators.note: top of means the first letter, the top in a down entry

explanation.surface: A wrap draped round the neck is a smoking-hot item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' suggests temperature, but is slang for pinched.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for goods that have been taken illegally and are risky to handle.

clue.text: Diffuse through cosmos eerily

indicators.note: through means the letters run inside the words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Seeping eerily across the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass gradually through a membrane, as liquids do, is to diffuse.

clue.text: Unnerves retired lieutenant, restrained by judges

indicators.note: restrained by means held in by, so the reversed piece sits inside

parts.note: to judge or assess is to rate

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A retired officer is shaken when held back by the court's judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake someone's composure is to make them nervous.

clue.text: Place fortune on American sports car

indicators.note: on means placed above in a down entry, so fortune comes first

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or fortune
US means American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: Betting a fortune on an American sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: A British maker of light, fast two-seaters; one of its models is this.

clue.text: Second taxi to refuse to come out

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A second taxi declines to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a strikebreaker, carrying on working when colleagues walk out.

clue.text: 'Railway Children' author endlessly recalled playwright

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is reversed
endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote the children's novel The Railway Children

explanation.surface: The novelist's work recalled endlessly by a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts NESBIT to NESBI and 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House, was a writer of plays.

clue.text: It's a grand sight in Venice and in France to this artist

parts.note: the Grand Canal is Venice's great waterway
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A Venetian view, and in France this painter gets credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' hints at the Grand Canal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century Venetian painter famous for vedute, views of his city.

clue.text: Dirty tricks investing thousand in finance company

indicators.note: investing means putting money in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: finance means money
K, from kilo, is a thousand
a business is a company

explanation.surface: Shady dealings as a firm invests a grand in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous or underhand behaviour, foolery or deceit.
